title: Universal Rule Schema 1.0.0
description: Domain-agnostic rule structure with deontic logic, adapter-based detection, and lineage tracking. Finding lifecycle states are documented in x-finding-fsm (informative; normative source: docs/spec/contracts/finding_lifecycle/).
x-normative-status: All x-* keys in this schema are informative and non-normative. docs/spec/contracts/ is the sole normative behavioral source.

changes: evaluator_type/evaluator_config replaced by detection_spec with adapter pattern
type field replaced by deontic field with expanded enum
subject field added (replaces implicit subject in evaluator hints)
predicate field added for deontic logic form
lineage_id pattern updated for universal taxonomy
schema_version field added as required constant
applicability field added for language/domain scoping
exclusions restructured to use pattern_category enum
domain_spec added for rule domain classification

x-cross-layer-binding.policy_runtime_role: Paired policy doctrine documents live in directives with the executable rule (dual-document Directive). They are read AFTER evaluation for guidance/reasoning via Directives Adapter and paired_policy_ref. NOT used for evaluation, inspection, or FSM transitions. No separate PolicyDoctrineReader.
x-cross-layer-binding.runtime_executable_source: docs/spec/contracts/conflict/ resolve_conflict over schema/CG-IR fields only
x-cross-layer-binding.rule: docs/spec/contracts/ is the normative behavioral source. Schema is a structural projection of contract invariants. Policy describes governance intent only.
x-cross-layer-binding.version_compatibility_math: A rule dataset with schema version S.S.S is compatible with policy version P.P.P if and only if major(S) == major(P). Formally: dataset(s) accepts policy(p) ⟺ ⌊s⌋ == ⌊p⌋. MINOR and PATCH differences are compatible within the same MAJOR family. A validator MUST reject datasets where major versions differ.
x-cross-layer-binding.adapter_pattern_note: Language-specific detection details belong ONLY in detection_spec.adapters[].adapter_config. The universal detection spec (structural_spec, semantic_spec, pattern_spec, composite_spec) MUST remain language-agnostic. Adapters translate abstract detection to concrete language-specific evaluators.
x-cross-layer-binding.policy_contract_version_check: JSON Schema cannot enforce that policy_contract_version matches the paired policy_doctrine_document version in directives. The compilation engine MUST reject directives where major(policy_contract_version) != major(doctrine.version) at compile time.
x-cross-layer-binding.audit_corpus: Formal verification audits MUST include docs/spec/contracts/, rule_schema.json, policy_doctrine.yaml, and docs/spec/README.md as the complete normative corpus. Archived prose lives under docs/spec/ARCHIVE_* for historical reference only.

x-discriminator-note.primary_discriminator: detection_spec.strategy determines which spec sub-object is active (structural_spec, semantic_spec, pattern_spec, composite_spec)
x-discriminator-note.adapter_discriminator: detection_spec.adapters[].target identifies the language/platform for each adapter; adapter_id references registered adapter implementation
x-discriminator-note.normative_gate: docs/spec/contracts/compilation/pipeline.yaml AST-walking detection.strategy discriminator is mandatory; engines relying on JSON Schema alone are non-conformant

x-finding-fsm.note: FSM is enforced at runtime by the Finding FSM Engine, not by JSON Schema structural validation of rule datasets.

x-portability-note.schema_limitation: JSON Schema structural validation is necessary but insufficient for cross-runtime determinism
compile_time_engine_invariants: RE2-compatible regex patterns only — PCRE features (backreferences, atomic groups) rejected by RE2 linter pass
NFC string normalization enforced before evaluator invocation
IEEE 754 finite doubles only — NaN and ±Infinity rejected in numeric fields
UTC-only timestamps — ISO 8601 with Z suffix; ±HH:MM offsets rejected
x-portability-note.enforcement: Reference validator and RE2 canary vectors are mandatory compile-time gates; see US-CP-002 and certification AA-07

x-cg-ir-hashing.dual_hash_model: semantic_hash (detection, scope, depends_on, priority, conflict_resolution, status, created_at) + presentation_hash (message, directive_revision, control_version) compose node_hash per docs/spec/contracts/compilation/pipeline.yaml
x-cg-ir-hashing.edge_hash: SHA-256 of sorted {source: directive_id, target: directive_id}
x-cg-ir-hashing.snapshot_hash: SHA-256 of sorted node_hashes + sorted edge_hashes + provenance
x-cg-ir-hashing.incremental_reuse: unchanged node_body produces identical node_hash across snapshots

contract.policy_mapping: Machine ID in directive tables maps to rule.lineage_id (immutable root). Execution ID maps to rule.id.
contract.spec_mapping: node.lineage_id in CG-IR maps to rule.lineage_id; node.directive_id maps to rule.id

x-identity.pattern_relationship: Execution ID pattern extends lineage_id pattern by appending zero or more -SUFFIX segments. Base pattern supports universal taxonomy prefixes (GOV, COD, SEC, INF, AIG, PROC, DAT, ACC, DOC). On first creation, execution_id equals lineage_id (zero suffixes). After fork/merge/split, suffixes appended. Suffix segments are hierarchical history tokens encoding the operation chain that produced the execution ID.

lifecycle.revision: Same lineage_id, same id, new revision. lineage field NOT required.
lifecycle.fork: Same lineage_id inherited, two new ids. lineage field REQUIRED.
lifecycle.merge: Merged lineage_id = lexicographic min of parent lineage_ids; new execution id per docs/spec/contracts/directive/identity.yaml. lineage field REQUIRED.
lifecycle.split: Same lineage_id inherited, multiple new ids. lineage field REQUIRED.
lifecycle.rename: Same lineage_id, same id. lineage field NOT required.
lifecycle.retire: Same lineage_id, same id, status=deprecated. lineage field NOT required.

invariants.lineage_id_immutable: Once assigned, lineage_id is never reused.
invariants.uniqueness: lineage_id MUST be unique within a ruleset.

x-deterministic-serialization.number_encoding: integer as integer, float as IEEE 754 double
x-deterministic-serialization.nan_policy: NaN and Infinity are NOT permitted in serializable objects
x-deterministic-serialization.hash_algorithm_versioning: Version 1: flat node_body hash (deprecated 8.2.0). Version 2: dual-hash model (semantic_hash + presentation_hash). If hash algorithm changes (e.g. SHA-256 → BLAKE3), increment hash_algorithm_version. All node_hash and snapshot_hash values MUST be recomputed. Old versions remain valid for audit replay but new compilations MUST use current version.
x-deterministic-serialization.canonical_form: All objects serialized with sorted keys before hashing
x-deterministic-serialization.recursive_structures: For recursive composite_spec: serialize components as array of canonical JSON objects. For lineage: serialize parent_*_ids as sorted arrays.
x-deterministic-serialization.schema_references: $ref resolved at schema validation time; not included in canonical form for hashing
x-deterministic-serialization.map_ordering: Objects with additionalProperties: keys sorted lexicographically before hashing
x-deterministic-serialization.normalization_rules: additionalProperties: true objects have keys sorted before hashing. Default values NOT injected into canonical form. Only explicit values participate in hashing.

inheritance.merge: Sorted-set union of all parent authored_by values

x-creator-provenance.enforcement: finding.waive denies if actor is in creator_provenance; finding.approve_remediation denies if actor submitted evidence

x-complexity-limits.not_chain_note: NOT composites (maxItems=1) may nest recursively up to max_composite_depth. Nested NOT chains (NOT(NOT(NOT(...))) are valid but semantically equivalent to a single NOT for odd depth or identity for even depth. Validators MAY warn on redundant NOT nesting.
x-complexity-limits.component_recursion: Composite components recurse via composite_spec.components. Each nesting level counts toward max_composite_depth. The reference validator MUST walk the full component tree, not only the root detection_spec.
x-complexity-limits.detection_node_counting: Each leaf detection component counts as 1 node. Composite detections count as 1 node plus the sum of their component nodes. Total across all rules in a dataset MUST NOT exceed max_detection_nodes_per_rule.

x-portable-validation.finite_numeric_required: All type:number fields MUST be finite (not NaN, not ±Infinity). Enforced at compile time by reference validator pre-pass, not JSON Schema alone.

x-conflict-resolution-binding.specificity_metric: docs/spec/contracts/conflict/precedence.yaml defines specificity as a composite score using scope_specificity_score and detection field binding. Two implementations MUST agree on specificity ranking for identical CG-IR node bodies.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.spec_model: Deterministic multi-factor: explicit override → compatible_overrides (symmetric pairs) → priority → specificity → recency
x-conflict-resolution-binding.schema_model: conflict_resolution field provides explicit override only; not a standalone algorithm
x-conflict-resolution-binding.precedence: Explicit override (conflict_resolution field) takes precedence over computed resolution. If no conflict_resolution field, spec multi-factor algorithm applies.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.cycle_handling: defer_to_cycle_detection via DFS (docs/spec/contracts/conflict/precedence.yaml): any directed cycle in defer_to subgraph causes all defer_to overrides to be ignored; fall through to computed resolution. If target rule in defer_to does not exist or is ambiguous (post-fork), the override is ignored; fall through to computed resolution.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.compatible_overrides: Symmetric pairs {always_wins, never_wins} and identical defer_to targets resolve deterministically per conflict/precedence compatible_overrides(). Incompatible dual overrides escalate to Conflict Artifact.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.defer_to_resolution: docs/spec/contracts/conflict/precedence.yaml defer_to_reference_resolution (normative): resolve to active rule by execution ID; follow lineage chain for deprecated targets; if multiple active children exist post-fork, escalate to Conflict Artifact
x-conflict-resolution-binding.scope_boundary: Conflict resolution applies within same lineage. Cross-lineage conflicts are flagged as Conflict Artifacts for human review.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.policy_model: Declarative intent description only. Compilation engine implements via spec multi-factor algorithm.

schema_version.description: Universal schema version. Breaks compatibility with pre-universal rule files (8.x.x). Migration required.

version.description: Directive graph version (semantic version of this rule dataset). Distinct from cg_ir_snapshot_hash in compilation/pipeline. MUST share the same MAJOR version as schema_version for compatibility.

policy_contract_version.description: Version of the paired policy_doctrine.yaml. Compile-time engine MUST verify major(policy_contract_version) == major(policy.version); JSON Schema cannot enforce cross-file version consistency.

policy_contract_id.description: Identifier of the paired policy contract.

metadata.description: Informational context only. MUST NOT contain executable hints. See docs/spec/contracts/directive/amendment.yaml.

upgrade_from.description: Previous dataset version this dataset was migrated from (e.g. '8.2.4').

upgrade_to.description: Target dataset version for next migration (e.g. '2.0.0').

migration_required.description: True if dataset requires manual migration steps before use with target version.

lineage_preservation.description: How lineage_ids are handled during migration.

merge_provenance.description: Explicit mapping of non-surviving parent lineage_ids during a merge operation. Mitigates lexicographic MIN provenance loss by documenting the semantic weight and context of each parent.

semantic_weight.description: Semantic importance of this parent in the merged rule.

context.description: Human-readable description of what the non-surviving parent contributed (e.g. 'payment processing rules', 'access control constraints').

merged_at.description: Timestamp of the merge operation. Optional for backward compatibility; strongly RECOMMENDED for audit trail completeness.

merge_notes.description: Additional context about the merge rationale.

rules.description: The list of directives. Every rule MUST have a unique lineage_id and id. Uniqueness enforced by external validator.

utc_datetime.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (Z suffix required). Offsets (±HH:MM) are rejected per compilation portable-validation and certification AA-07.

deontic_modality.description: Deontic logic modality defining the normative force of the directive

subject_category.description: What category of unit the rule governs - abstract, not language-specific

exclusion_pattern_category.description: Universal category of exclusion - applies across all languages and domains

paired_policy_ref.description: Reference to the paired policy doctrine document that provides guidance, reasoning, and examples for this rule. Used AFTER evaluation to generate human/AI-facing guidance.

structural_spec.description: For structural strategy - describes WHAT to look for without language specifics

forbidden_patterns.description: Abstract pattern descriptions that violate the rule

flags.description: Pattern flags - names must be universal, not language-specific regex flags

composite_spec.description: For composite strategy - combines other rules/detections

rule_ref.description: Reference to another rule's lineage_id or id

external_spec.description: For external strategy - delegates to external detection tool

manual_spec.description: For manual strategy - human review required

review_criteria.description: Criteria for human reviewers to check

adapters.description: Implementation adapters - maps abstract detection spec to concrete evaluators. THIS is where language-specific config lives.

target.description: What this adapter targets - examples: python-ast, javascript-ast, rust-hir, terraform-hcl, openapi-spec, yaml-config, json-config, markdown-docs, prompt-template

adapter_id.description: Identifier of the adapter implementation registered in the system

adapter_config.description: Adapter-specific configuration - this is the ONLY place language-specific details belong

overrides.description: Target-specific overrides to the universal spec

applicability.description: Where and when this rule applies

artifact_types.description: Types of artifacts this rule applies to (e.g., source-code, test-code, configuration, infrastructure-as-code, prompt-template, workflow-definition)

mode.description: universal=applies to all languages; include=only listed languages; exclude=all except listed

languages.description: Language identifiers when mode is include or exclude

context_scope.description: Execution contexts (e.g., production, staging, development, ci-cd)

scope_description.description: Human-readable description of what is excluded

schema_version.description: Universal schema version constant. Confirms this rule uses the universal schema.

lineage_id.description: Immutable rule identifier. Prefix indicates domain: GOV (cross-cutting), COD (coding), SEC (security), INF (infrastructure), AIG (AI governance), PROC (process), DAT (data governance), ACC (access control), DOC (documentation)

id.description: Active execution identifier. May change on fork/merge/split. Used for CG-IR compilation.

predicate.description: What must/must not be true about the subject - the normative claim in deontic logic form

principles.description: References to universal principles this rule operationalizes (e.g., determinism, localized-failure, explicit-over-implicit, fail-safe-defaults, validation-as-contract, resource-ownership-explicit, single-truth-source)

anchor_ref.description: Link back to policy document. section: refs or JSON Pointer per docs/spec/contracts/directive/amendment.yaml. JSON Pointer format follows RFC 6901.

directive_revision.description: Revision identifier of the source directive (e.g. 'v3', '2026-07-05-r2'). Maps to CG-IR node.directive_revision.

control_version.description: Version of evaluation logic for this rule. Maps to CG-IR node.control_version.

scope.description: Structured applicability context. Replaces bare target string for deterministic scope filtering and specificity scoring per docs/spec/contracts/conflict/precedence.yaml.

filters.description: Additional applicability filter predicates on target metadata or content.

field.description: Path within target metadata or content.

metadata.description: Per-rule metadata. Informational only — MUST NOT contain executable hints. See docs/spec/contracts/directive/amendment.yaml. metadata.audit.authored_by is required for active rules and compiled to creator_provenance per finding_lifecycle/sod_contract.

authored_by.description: Actor ID of directive creator. Inherited through lineage operations. Compiled to creator_provenance for segregation enforcement.

depends_on.description: IDs of rules that must be evaluated first.

conflicts_with.description: IDs of rules that cannot coexist.

conflict_resolution.description: Explicit conflict resolution override. Takes precedence over computed resolution per docs/spec/contracts/conflict/precedence.yaml.

defer_to.description: Rule ID to defer to (required if strategy=defer_to)

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Participates in conflict resolution recency step (docs/spec/contracts/conflict/precedence.yaml).

lineage.description: Tracks identity lifecycle operations. REQUIRED for fork, merge, split. NOT required for revision, rename, retire.

parent_lineage_ids.description: Immutable root IDs of parent directives. Cardinality: fork/split=1, merge=2.

parent_execution_ids.description: Active execution IDs of parent directives at time of operation. Cardinality matches parent_lineage_ids.
